title: neex.json
description: Configuration for neex, the polyglot monorepo task runner. At the workspace root it configures tasks for every project; inside a project directory it declares that project's tasks and dependencies.

projects.description: Root only. Extra project globs added to what the language providers discover (e.g. directories that only have a neex.json). `!` excludes.

globalEnv.description: Root only. Env var names whose values are part of every task's cache key. A trailing `*` matches a prefix.

globalInputs.description: Root only. Root-relative globs whose contents are part of every task's cache key.

name.description: Project file only. Overrides the project's name.

deps.description: Project file only. Other projects this one depends on, by name, ecosystem id, or path. This is how a cross-language dependency is declared.

tasks.description: Keys: `build` (every project), `web#build` (one project), `//#format` (a root task). In a project file, a value may be just a command string.

dependsOn.description: `^build` = build in upstream projects first, `codegen` = a task in the same project, `proto#generate` = a specific project's task.

inputs.description: Project-relative globs that make up the task's file inputs. Default: every non-ignored file in the project. Positive globs restrict, `!` excludes, `//path` adds a root-relative file.

outputs.description: Project-relative globs stored after a successful run and restored on a cache hit. `!` excludes.

env.description: Env var names whose values are part of the cache key. A trailing `*` matches a prefix.

passThroughEnv.description: Env vars available to the task but NOT part of the cache key. Changing them never invalidates the cache, so use sparingly.

cache.description: Cache this task's results. Default: true for tasks mentioned in neex.json and for build/test/lint/check/typecheck; false otherwise.

persistent.description: A long-running task such as a dev server. Never cached; nothing may depend on it.

command.description: Shell command for this task. Only valid for `project#task`, `//#task`, and in project files.
